the horizontal transfer of microRNAs via ingestion of food is not a general phenomenon and that it is highly dependent on the specific characteristics of the microRNA.

, although the possibility that microRNAs are transferred from mother to offspring via the milk is still open, the present study demonstrates that the oral ingestion of a high level of a microRNA in mouse milk does not affect the level of this microRNA in the pup tissues.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oral ingestion of microRNAs does not lead to an increase of their level in the tissues of the recipients.
, in the absence of a strong and specific target, miR-30 is unlikely to be horizontally transferred and to regulate the expression of a target in the tissues of the pups.
the oral delivery of miRNAs from milk to the pups is not efficient, at least for the microRNA we have studied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we did not detect a significant increase of miR- 30b in the liver, heart, lung and brain of pups fed by miR-30-transgenic mice compared to pups fed with wild-type milk.
the presence of high levels of miRNAs in milk does not necessarily lead to a transfer and accumulation of the miRNAs in the pups.
the transfer of microRNAs from mother to offspring via oral ingestion of milk does not appear to be an efficient way to deliver miRNAs to tissues.
